title: High-throughput Screening and Characterization of Small-Molecule Inhibitors of N-Terminal Autoproteolysis of Coronavirus Main Protease Precursors
text:
Coronaviruses—including SARS-CoV-2, MERS-CoV, and several common cold strains—encode a main
protease (Mpro) that is initially produced as part of larger polyprotein precursors and activated through
precursor-mediated autoproteolysis. This project aims to develop novel inhibitors that selectively block
this conserved precursor autoprocessing step, offering mechanisms distinct from current Mpro inhibitors
that target the active site of mature enzyme. By inhibiting both precursor and mature Mpro, this approach
could enable complementary combination therapies and improve the overall effectiveness of antiviral
treatments against a a broad range of coronaviruses.

title: SOSIP trimer production and supply
text: Core B Abstract The role of the SOSIP Trimer Production and Supply Core (Core B) is to support the work of the Research Projects by making appropriate quantities of high quality, soluble envelope glycoprotein trimers and related reagents. The Core will then supply the Project Leaders and external collaborators, and other scientists who request access to our reagents. The Core will also share its knowhow and provide training, quality control and trouble-shooting services to the team. Dr. John P. Moore will be Core Leader. Mr. Albert Cupo will direct the Core’s activities on a day-to-day basis. The Core is located at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York City. The tasks of the Core are outlined below. Other responsibilities related to the production of trimers and other relevant reagents may arise during the life of the award and will be accomplished as and when appropriate. Aim 1: To produce milligram quantities of high quality SOSIP trimers in mammalian cells by transient transfection. The Core will use ExpiCHO cells to produce appropriate amounts of trimers designed and evaluated by the Project 1 and 2 teams. The trimers will be assessed for purity and antigenic quality, then supplied to the projects and to key collaborators. The Core will evaluate and use new trimer stabilization methods, such as the dPG mutation to gp41 that can improve the yields or properties of tagged trimers used to analyze ongoing clinical trials, and of trimers from the 9-virus global Tier-2 neutralization panel that are candidate polishing immunogens for gl-bNAb lineages initiated by the GT1.1 trimer. Aim 2: To create and use permanent cell lines expressing SOSIP trimers. The Core will use its established methods to make stable CHO cell lines expressing wild-type or epitope-tagged SOSIP trimers from various genotypes, under non-GMP conditions, when larger amounts are needed. New lines will include ones producing improved trimers for clinical trial analyses that were initially evaluated in Aim 1. Aim 3: To supply and advise external requestors of SOSIP trimer reagents. Over the past decade, the Core has supplied purified SOSIP trimers, expression plasmids and stable cell lines to well over 100 different research groups world-wide. The effort expended in providing these unrestricted gifts has been substantial. We anticipate, and will plan for, a continuation of this service to the HIV-1 vaccine and virology research communities. By providing a central service to both Research Projects, and external collaborators, the Trimer Production Core will be intimately involved in the scientific program of the entire HIVRAD grant-funded team.

title: Natural history of multisystem proteinopathy-1
text: (Project 4: Natural History of MSP1) This proposal’s primary objective is to validate a promising measure of motor function as a future efficacy out- come in a large cohort of patients with multisystem proteinopathy 1 (MSP1) due to a pathogenic missense vari- ant in the valosin-containing protein (VCP) gene. Secondarily, we will establish the temporal course with which different phenotypic manifestations of MSP1 emerge and explore how these impact performance of clinical out- come assessments (COA), including our primary outcome the North Star Assessment for limb girdle-type Dys- trophies (NSAD). We hypothesize that this multicenter study will define an expected trajectory of disease pro- gression, quantify the impact of covariates on progression, and establish thresholds for meaningful change in MSP1. The VCP protein has been viewed as a tractable therapeutic target by industry. Small molecule inhibi- tors and activators exist, and some are in clinical trials for other diseases (i.e. blood cancers and solid tissue tumors). These compounds have shown promise by correcting disease phenotypes in pre-clinical models that include human derived motor neurons and mouse models. Other therapeutic approaches include allele spe- cific knockdown and gene editing platforms both of which have been performed in pre-clinical studies. While all these advances are promising, the current understanding of the underlying causes of disease heterogene- ity, including the genotype/phenotype relationships, impact of phenoconversion on trajectory of progression, and incomplete penetrance of other body system involvement even among sibling pairs add to the complexity of clinical trial planning in this ultra-rare disease. Thus, the need to prospectively characterize a large cohort of patients with MSP1 across a multisite consortium with sites distributed across the United States, United King- dom, and South Africa. The specific aims of our proposal are to (1) Validate the NSAD as a primary efficacy outcome to characterize the progression of motor dysfunction in MSP1, (2) Evaluate the emergence and im- pact of other system involvement on performance of motor COA, and (3) Establish a biorepository of longitudi- nal specimens from deeply-phenotyped MSP1 patients for future biomarker discovery. To achieve these aims, we propose to prospectively follow 80 patients with MSP1 over at least 2 years. Detailed training of at least two clinical evaluators from each collaborating site will take place at the lead institution, Nationwide Children’s Hos- pital, before enrollment with annual refresher trainings. MSP1 is ultra-rare, and travel is burdensome. There- fore, we also selected geographically diverse locations to minimize travel and burden of trial participation. Re- mote assessments have been validated as a testing method, which further reduces burden of participation with fewer onsite visits required. Our partnerships with advocacy groups, including Cure VCP Disease and the Mus- cular Dystrophy Association, will allow us to successfully recruit patients. Completion of our aims will result in a validated measure of meaningful change in motor function, an understanding of the impact of phenotypic pene- trance and changes in biomarkers on measurement of disease progression to achieve clinical trial readiness in this cohort.

title: Point-of-care Nucleic Acid Amplification Test for pangenomic Hepatitis C diagnosis in outpatient clinics
text:
Hepatitis C is a widely prevalent bloodborne viral infection that may lead to chronic liver disease and accounts
for an estimated 1.1 million annual global deaths. Within the last six years, direct acting antivirals have
demonstrated high cure rates across all genotypes in 8 to 12 weeks of all-oral treatment; however, the lack of
nucleic acid amplification tests available to outpatient clinics has hampered the ability to link patients to available
treatment and confirm their viral suppression after treatment. We propose to develop and validate a point-of-
care, pan-genomic Hepatitis C nucleic acid test that can provide results in less than 30 minutes and be used by
untrained users in a wide range of outpatient clinical settings.

title: A precision tumor neoantigen identification pipeline for cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-based cancer immunotherapies
text:
Development of vaccines and other immunotherapies to direct cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL)-mediated
elimination of cancers will impact global health significantly. This proposal establishes an integrative service for
end users to identify those CTL targets with precision in order to harness a focused and personalized immune
offensive against cancer.

title: Tumor Metabolic Profiling by Multiplexed Single-Cell Lipid and mRNA Imaging
text:
To survive in the nutrient- and oxygen-deprived tumor microenvironment (TME), cancer cells undergo a drastic
metabolic reprogramming where they upregulate both their endogenous lipid synthesis and exogenous uptake
of lipids. Although this altered lipid metabolism has the potential to serve as a powerful diagnostic approach and
research tool in cancer biology, current methods to evaluate lipid profiles are unable to provide single-cell
analysis and lack spatial precision. Here, we describe a unique platform for lipid profiling of cancer and cancer-
associated cells in intact tissue samples at single-cell level by probing inherent molecular vibrations using
spectral coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS) microscopy, simultaneously with RNA imaging by
stimulated Raman excited fluorescence (SREF).

title: Targeting the Epigenetic and Metabolic Control of EBV-Epithelial Cancers
text:
OVERALL - PROJECT NARRATIVE
This is a new program project that brings together experts in Epstein-Barr Virus latency, epigenetics, metabolism,
and carcinogenesis with core expertise in medicinal chemistry, drug discovery, bioinformatics, and animal
models of EBV cancer. The overall goal is to address the unmet medical need associated with EBV epithelial
cancers that exceed 180,000 new cancer cases per year and receive generic, non-viral cancer treatments and
have high rates of failure, relapse and resistance. The Program brings together multiple institutions and
collaborators to elucidate the basic mechanisms of viral latency and oncogenesis in EBV epithelial cancers, and
to identify vulnerabilities and strategies for development of new viral-specific therapies to treat EBV epithelial
cancers.

title: Functional Genomics Training Program (FGTP)
text:
This application describes a training program in Functional Genomics. Our program provides predoctoral
trainees with the conceptual and technical foundation for developing independent careers in basic and
translational genetics and genomics. The training supports the overall mission of NIGMS to promote
research that increases understanding of biological processes and lays the foundation for advances in
disease diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.

title: Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring in Bacteria of Veterinary Significance
text:
Emergence of antibiotic resistance continues to be a threat to both human and animal health around the world,
and this burden can be reduced with the prudent use of antibiotics through culture and susceptibility testing.
The AHDC Bacteriology laboratory is engaged to continue its cooperative agreement with the FDA Vet-LIRN to
promote the areas of food and feed surveillance, antibiotic susceptibility testing, quality management, animal
health, food safety, and food security. As a continued participant in the Vet-LIRN network of veterinary
diagnostic laboratories, the AHDC Bacteriology laboratory can provide surge capacity for large-scale testing in
the event of an emergency.

title: Role of cortical GABAergic interneurons in psychedelic drug action
text:
Classical psychedelics such as psilocybin are being investigated as potential treatment for major depression. It
is known that psilocybin can induce neural plasticity in the neocortex, however the brain region contains many
different cell types and how they may interact to mediate drug action is not known. This proposal seeks to
address this knowledge gap, which can provide insights into the neurobiology of psilocybin and may lead to
better treatments for depression.

title: Diabetic Memory in Hematopoietic Stem Cells
text:
Gestational diabetes is a common medical complication of pregnancy that annually affects ~250,000 women in
the United States. Diabetes exposure during pregnancy can have long-term consequences on the health of
offspring as it is associated with an increased risk of developing metabolic (obesity and type-2 diabetes) and
cardiovascular diseases. The proposed research will investigate the
hematopoietic alterations in offspring born
to diabetic pregnancies to provide new diagnostic and therapeutic tools to mitigate the long-term negative effects
of gestational diabetes on the health of adult offspring.

title: The regulatory landscape of segmentally duplicated genes:  Implications for human evolution and disease
text:

title: Dyadic and social network influences on health and well-being among young adults with cancer
text:
Social challenges are a major issue for young adult couples coping with cancer. Impairments in their social
relationships may decrease their relationship satisfaction and well-being and disrupt their physiological stress
axis activity (dysregulation). This study will use innovative methods (social network analysis, ecological
momentary assessment, salivary bioscience) to examine interrelationships between young adult couples’
communication, both within (couple) and outside (social network) their social relationships, and between the
structure and composition of their social networks, on relationship satisfaction, well-being, and physiological
biomarkers of stress among both members of the dyad to inform targeted interventions that foster the long-term
health and well-being of young adult couples coping with cancer.

title: Integrated Host-Microbe Metagenomics for Sepsis Pathogen Surveillance, Subphenotyping and Outcome Prediction
text:
Sepsis is a leading cause of in-hospital mortality and involves a heterogeneous and dysregulated host immune
response to infection. This proposal seeks to advance our understanding and management of sepsis by profiling
the immune response and detecting microbial pathogens in blood samples from 1,563 patients enrolled in the
multicenter CLOVERS trial, using a technique called metagenomic sequencing. Together, this work will achieve
the following specific aims: 1) understand the microbial causes of sepsis, 2) identify subgroups of sepsis patients
with distinct immunologic and microbiologic characteristics that may be uniquely treatment-responsive, and 3)
develop a novel molecular blood test to accurately predict sepsis outcomes.

title: Cellular and Molecular Mechanisms of Atherosclerosis
text:
Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide and substantial
residual CVD risk persists despite effective LDL-cholesterol (LDL-C) lowering. In this context, we propose an
investigation of mechanisms of plaque stabilization and destabilization focused on novel functions of vascular
macrophages and stromal cells, and their crosstalk, in mouse models and human CVD. Our overarching
theme, pursued through three highly integrated Projects and two Scientific Cores is that inflammation and the
efferocytosis-resolution cycle in macrophages regulates plaque stability through crosstalk with other
macrophages and stromal cells and that detailed examination of the cell and molecular mechanisms may provide
opportunities for novel CVD treatments, including in patients with clonal hematopoiesis, an emerging CVD risk
factor.

title: Cortical Integration in Humans: An Intracranial Investigation of Neural Synchrony
text:
Disruptions in cortical integration are associated with a variety of neurological and psychiatric disorders that
are poorly understood and urgently need better treatment options, such as schizophrenia, dementia, ADHD,
and many more. Furthermore, due to ethical reasons, much of the research that is performed to study the basic
neurophysiology underlying these diseases is performed in rodents. Developing a better understanding of the
human neurophysiology underlying the processes which are disrupted is essential to developing efficacious
treatments for them and the research highlighted in this proposal has the potential to inform such models and
treatments.

title: The impact of inflammation on HSPC composition and disease progression in chronic myelomonocytic leukemia
text:
The conventional clinical management strategy for patients with chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) is to
initiate therapy at the time of disease progression and clonal evolution. In this project, we will determine whether
inflammatory insults can drive a specific evolutionary adaption known as the `mono-biased' state and disease
progression. Importantly, we will determine if this inflammation dependent effect can be mitigated by existing
therapeutics and cytokine inhibitors leading to a paradigm shift in CMML management whereby these therapies
can be deployed in a clinically asymptomatic state to prevent disease progression.

title: Real-time Perfusion Imaging Guided Bone Debridement in Fracture Related Infection - A Precision Approach to Debridement
text:
Despite the strong relationship between low post-debridement bone perfusion and early (<3 month)
infection recurrence demonstrated in our initial funding period in patients with Fracture Related
Infection, no intraoperative strategies currently exist to guide and optimize surgical debridement. In
this proposal, we will refine our fluorescence guided debridement (FGD) imaging system to an
optimized, surgeon-centered, operating-room ready tool, evaluate how real-time intraoperative
visualization of quantitative perfusion data using the FGD intervention influences surgeons’
debridement decisions, and assess the usability and acceptability of the device across five sites.
Upon completion, we will be positioned to conduct a pivotal Phase III randomized controlled trial
comparing FGD with standard of care, anticipating that integration of FGD into surgical practice will
reduce treatment failures, reduce the number of required surgical procedures and establish new
benchmarks in surgical care.

title: Developing an autism-specific mortality risk index using data from Medicare-enrolled autistic older adults
text:
High risk for premature mortality is one of the most pressing issues faced by the growing population of autistic
older adults but the absence of accurate autism-specific mortality risk prediction tools results in inability to
systematically identify those at the highest risk for targeted intervention. This proposal will have a high public
health impact by providing critical information about detecting mortality risk among autistic older adults that can
ultimately be used to improve life-expectancy among autistic people. This proposal is well-aligned with the NIA’s
Strategic Plan, as we seek to “understand disparities related to aging and [inform] strategies to improve the
health status of older adults” on the autism spectrum, and NOT-AG-21-020 in that we will analyze existing
Medicare claims data to examine “subgroups of older adults with special needs” and “health outcomes in complex
multimorbid older adults.”

title: Development of a versatile paired prime editing toolkit for CFTR gene correction
text:
Genome editing techniques can correct the defective genes at their native locus and permanently restore the
gene function, potentially providing a one-time curative treatment for genetic diseases. This study aims to
engineer a generalized gene correction toolkit to address the broad spectrum of disease-causing CFTR
mutations and explore its therapeutic applications in vivo. Findings from this work will pave the way for a gene
therapy strategy for cystic fibrosis as well as various genetic diseases with high allelic heterogeneity.
